title: 62chan
description: An imageboard about the Signal on 62. Registrar offshore, moderator gone since August 2024, roughly eighteen bot posts for every human one.

threads.subject: heard it again last night, ashkettle cut
threads.body:
[img:photo:62-cut-dashboard]

pulled off at the quarry cut around 11. same woman. 4 digits at a time. radio in the truck picks it up on the AM band which should not be possible but it does

first time in like a year I actually stopped and listened all the way through

posts.body:
AM band pickup in the cut is almost certainly your radio, not the transmission. A strong signal into a cheap front end will produce a detectable envelope in a receiver that has no business hearing it. It happens in that cut specifically because of terrain gain plus the fact that you are in a metal box under a rock wall.

If you want to test it: drive 300m west, out of the cut, and try again. It will vanish. That does not mean the Signal stopped. It means your radio did.

Timing, for your log: carrier up around :06:45, groups start :07:00.
did the 300m thing. gone. came back when I reversed. that's kind of a relief honestly

threads.subject: RECEPTION LOG THREAD - method, equipment, raw data, no speculation
threads.body:
Starting this because every other thread on this board is people telling each other what it is, and nobody is writing down what it does.

[b]Equipment.[/b] Software defined receiver, 14 bit. Two element directional at 9 metres on a mast, rotatable, bearing logged per observation. Calibrated against two known broadcast stations each session before logging.

[b]Method.[/b] Every odd hour local, 19:00 through 05:00. Session runs from :00 to :20. I log: frequency, bearing, S-meter, local weather, and whether groups were readable.

[b]What I will not do in this thread.[/b] Speculate. If you want to know what I think it is, the answer is that I do not know what it is.

[b]What I want from you.[/b] Bearings from other locations. Two bearings is a line. Three is a fix. I have one.

posts.body: this is the only good post on this board

[b]Feb 2020 summary.[/b] 28 sessions, 27 detections. One null, 14 Feb, heavy sleet, almost certainly propagation and not the transmitter.

Carrier onset: mean :06:47, standard deviation 1.9 seconds. That is the tightest number in the whole log and it is the one that tells you this is a machine on a clock.
sd of 1.9 seconds over 27 sessions is insane. nothing a person is doing looks like that

[b]2020 annual.[/b] 337 sessions. 328 detections. Nine nulls, eight of them weather.

No change in schedule. No change in voice. No change in group length. Nothing in 2020 happened to it.
have you tried asking on the old county board? there are people on there who were listening to this in the 90s

Yes. The 1998 thread is the earliest documentation I have found anywhere and it is still readable: [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url]

The description in 1998 matches what I recorded last night. Same schedule, same format, same voice. That is twenty-eight years of a machine not changing.

"I still do not know what it is" - four years, a thousand sessions, and he still writes that line every time. respect

I want to record something else while I am here. This year my log got scraped, run through something, and published on three sites as evidence for three different explanations, two of which contradict each other and one of which contradicts the log itself. One of them quotes me as having "confirmed" a military origin. I have never used the word military in this thread. You can search it.

I am going to keep posting the raw numbers because the raw numbers are the only thing that cannot be argued with, and because in forty years somebody is going to want them and there will not be anybody left who was doing this.

A copy goes to the library in Marchfield every March. Paper and disc. They catalogue it, which means it exists.

threads.subject: map thread - post your bearings
threads.body:
Two bearings is a line. Three is a fix. I have two, seven years apart, from Ashkettle and Halsey.

If you are more than 20km from either and you have a directional antenna, post: your approximate location, your antenna, your bearing, and the date and time. Approximate location is fine. I do not want your address and you should not post it.

[b]I will take a bad bearing over no bearing. Just say it is bad.[/b]

posts.body: I have a loop on a balcony in New Carrow. is that useless
No. A loop gives you a null, which is a bearing with an ambiguity. Two nulls from different places resolve each other. Post it.
New Carrow, small loop, null at roughly 310/130, 2022-09-05 2307 local. probably bad, I rotated it by hand

Logged. Thank you. It is consistent with the Ashkettle line within about 8 degrees, which for a hand-rotated loop on a balcony is honestly better than I expected.

That is three. It is a fix. It is a long way from here.
how far

Far enough that it was never ours, and close enough that I am not going to post the number on a public board and send somebody with a shovel to a stranger's field on the strength of three amateur bearings.

I have sent the full working to two people who asked for it properly and can check my arithmetic. Neither of them agreed with all of it. That is what it is for.
